overview: FAM4701 is a flight event focused on ocf recovery procedures. The notes below are organized off the canonical syllabus items first, then filled out with local FAM gouge so students can brief the event, explain the why behind each item, and stay ahead of instructor follow-up questions.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

children.text: Description:
Know the entry airspeed, altitude, configuration, and cockpit setup before you start the maneuver.
Aircraft is unresponsive to normal control inputs
Caused by a stalled condition where inertial forces exceed aerodynamic control authority
Controls may feel ineffective or act in reverse
Common Causes:
Failing to reduce power/deploy speed brake
Not reporting oil pressure
Inverted:
Roll to the nearest horizon (shortest distance)
Power as req.
As nose approaches/slightly above horizon, check/report oil pressure
Adjust power to maintain flight
Not rolling in shortest distance to horizon
Use ~4 Gs to smoothly recover to level flight
As airspeed/Gs increase (~4 Gs), perform AGSM
Raise nose to ~10° pitch.
Stay inverted only within NATOPS time limit.
Raise gear
At ≥110 KIAS, raise flaps
A torque setting above 60% in the stall can induce a left torque roll. Full right rudder and aileron may not prevent departure. Be especially cautious during power-on turning stalls.
If in a low energy state with AOA <18.0 and airspeed too low to sustain level flight, apply power cautiously. If in an unrecoverable descent, EJECT if below 6000’ AGL.
Stick shaker typically activates at 15.5 units AOA, which corresponds to 5–10 KIAS above stall in unaccelerated flight.
Common Errors
Warnings:
Note clock and check oil pressure immediately.
recovery from NH, NL, or Inverted attitudes due to disorientation, misflown maneuvers, or external factors. Recovery is visual (VFR) and must be completed above 6000’ AGL
Nose-High:
PCL - MAX (if low airspeed)
Use back stick to bring nose to horizon
Roll upright as nose approaches horizon
Roll wings level, raise nose, check oil pressure, power as req.
Not setting PCL to MAX at low airspeed
Pushing forward stick (zero or -Gs)
Stopping roll with nose still above horizon
Nose-Low:
Roll to nearest horizon
If needed, allow nose below horizon to regain airspeed
UA recovery does not work if stalled or in OCF
Use back stick to bring nose to horizon
NOTE: avoid knife-edge; roll past 90° and use +G
Common Errors:
never push over with forward stick (induces 0/-G)
avoid knife-edge; roll past 90° and use +G
stick shaker/buffet = imminent stall - reduce back pressure
Warnings:
All Aerobatic Maneuvers is judged by how well you enter it, stay ahead of the aircraft, and recover without needing cleanup coaching.
Setup / entry
Flown as one continuous evolution.
Thoroughly brief maneuver order and energy management plan with IP before execution.
Execute:
All Aerobatic Maneuvers is judged by how well you enter it, stay ahead of the aircraft, and recover without needing cleanup coaching.
Know the entry airspeed, altitude, configuration, and cockpit setup before you start the maneuver.
Standards / numbers
Choose and sequence up to 4 aerobatic maneuvers (e.g., Loop → Half Cuban Eight → Immelmann → Split-S).
Common errors / grading traps
The usual trap is missing the setup picture, then trying to salvage All Aerobatic Maneuvers late.
